swap_risks: CRITICAL SUPPLY VOLTAGE RATING: LMV358IDR is limited to 5.5 V max (5.5 V abs max, p.5) whereas LM358DR supports up to 30 V (32 V abs max, p.4). Installing a 5.5 V CMOS op-amp on a 12 V–24 V rail causes instant breakdown.

HIGH HEADROOM / CLIPPING RISK: Rail-to-rail capability differs (LM358DR: IN=Non-RR, OUT=Non-RR vs LMV358IDR: IN=Non-RR, OUT=RR); verify input common-mode range (Vicm) and output voltage swing against ADC full-scale range.
CAUTION SLEW RATE DIFFERENCE: Slew rate differs by 3.3x (LM358DR: 0.3 V/µs p.10 vs LMV358IDR: 1 V/µs p.7); check full-power bandwidth SR / (2π·Vpeak).
CAUTION THERMAL MARGIN: Package θJA differs by 40% (LM358DR: 124.7 °C/W p.5 vs LMV358IDR: 207.9 °C/W p.6); re-check Tj = Ta + Pd × θJA against Tj,max.
engineering_verdict: LM358DR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) and LMV358IDR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required replacements: while the footprint is physically compatible, engineering review and passive/circuit adjustments are mandatory due to supply voltage Vs,max drops >20%; rail-to-rail input/output swing differs; slew rate differs >= 3x. Key datasheet deltas: device type is opamp (push-pull) vs opamp (push-pull), supply limit is 30 V (p.5) vs 5.5 V (p.5), max Vos is 7 mV (p.10) vs 7 mV (p.7), input bias current is 20000 pA (p.10) vs 15000 pA (p.7), and Iq/ch is 350 µA (p.10) vs 105 µA (p.7). Always validate pinout orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.3), thermal margin (θJA 124.7 vs 207.9 °C/W), and official manufacturer datasheets on hardware prototypes before production release.
